now adverb

at present

also at the moment, at present, for now, for the time being, from now on, even now, here and now, even today, still now, now … now, now at last

classical

Catull. 4.25–26: sed haec prius fuēre: nunc …
Liv. 21.54.2: nunc corpora cūrāre tempus est
Traupman 88

nunc

adverb

now, at present

The present as against before or after: prius … nunc, nunc … ōlim.

Other words

  • jam — now (by now, at last); in a moment

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. And. 3.4.2: jam advesperāscit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 88: now, nunc; (denoting emphasis and urgency) jam

    Jam marks a point reached: what is so now and was not before (jam advesperāscit, it’s getting dark now), or, with a future, what is about to happen (see in a moment).

  • in praesentiā — for now, at the moment, for the time being

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 15.20.4: hoc videō in praesentiā opus esse (Lewis & Short); Cic. Tusc. 5.100

  • posthāc — from now on, in future

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 3.28 (Lewis & Short); Ter. Eun. 5.2.59 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 87: hereafter, posthāc

    numquam posthāc, never again (see never).

  • etiamnum (etiamnunc) — even now, still, even today

    also used · classical · Traupman 310

    Lewis & Short: etiamnunc is the more frequent form, and the only one in Cicero and Caesar.

  • dēpraesentiārum — here and now, at present

    avoid · classical · Petr. 58.3, 74.17 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 87; Traupman 327

    (vōx sermōnis vulgāris: Petr.)

    Lewis & Short find it only in two speeches of Petronius' freedmen. Say nunc or in praesentiā.

Examples

  • sed haec prius fuēre: nunc recondita senet quiēte

    but all that was before: now it is laid up and grows old in peaceCatull. 4.25–26

  • nunc corpora cūrāre tempus est

    now is the time to look after ourselvesLiv. 21.54.2

  • nōn, sī male nunc, et ōlim sīc erit

    if things are bad now, they will not always be soHor. C. 2.10.17–18

  • veniam ad cēnam, sed jam nunc pacīscor, sit expedīta sit parca

    I’ll come to dinner, but I’m setting my terms now: let it be quick, let it be frugalPlin. Ep. 3.12.1

  • etiam nunc

    even nowTraupman 352

  • modo … modo

    now … nowTraupman 352

See also just now, at once, in a moment, today, already, moment.
